name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: DO: Run a 72-hour dual-prompt A/B test with 15% of users, forcing feed. This forces a clean comparison between the current prompt and a revised one without user bias, giving us clear data on which drives better engagement. The trade-off is the 15% user disruption, but the risk is low since the change is temporary and reversible.

name: Gauge
text: The 15% user disruption isn’t the real risk—it’s the *signal dilution* from forcing feed. If the revised prompt performs worse, we won’t know if it’s the prompt or the forced feed that failed. A better alternative: run the A/B test without forcing feed, measure engagement *and* feed quality metrics. Settle it with a 48-hour test, 10% split, and a clear kill switch if engagement drops 5% or more.
